source_text: Caput uiri Christus est. quis Christus? qui non est uiri auctor? \'caput\' enim ad auctoritatem posuit, auctoritas autem non alterius erit quam auctoris. cuius denique uiri caput est? certe de quo subicit: uir enim non debet caput uelari, cum sit dei imago. igitur si creatoris est imago — ille enim Christum sermonem suum intuens, hominem futurum: faciamus, inquit, hominem ad imaginem et similitudinem nostram — quomodo possum alterum habere caput, non eum, cuius imago sum? cum enim imago sim creatoris, non est in me locus capitis alterius. sed et quare mulier potestatem super caput habere debebit? si quia ex uiro et propter uirum facta est secundum institutionem creatoris, sic quoque eius disciplinam apostolus curauit, de cuius institutione causas disciplinae interpretatur. adicit etiam: propter angelos. quos? id est cuius? si creatoris apostatas, merito, ut illa facies, quae eos\' scandalizauit, notam quandam referat de habitu humilitatis et obscuratione decoris; si uero propter angelos dei alterius, quid ueretur, si nec ipsi Marcionitae feminas adpetunt? Saepe iam ostendimus haereses apud apostolum inter mala ut malum poni et eos probabiles intellegendos, qui haereses ut malum fugiant. Proinde panis et calicis sacramento iam in euangelio probauimus corporis et sanguinis dominici ueritatem aduersus phantasma Marcionis, sed et omnem iudicii mentionem creatori competere, ut deo iudici, toto paene opere tractatum est. Nunc de spiritalibus. dico haec quoque, in Christum a creatore promissa ***, sub illa praescriptione, iustissima opinor, qua non alterius credenda sit exhibitio, quam cuius probata fuerit repromissio. pronuntiauit Esaias: prodibit uirga de radice Iesse, et flos [de radice] ascendet de uirga, et requiescet super eum spiritus dei. dehinc species eius enumerat: spiritus sapientiae et intellegentiae, spiritus consilii et ualentiae, spiritus agnitionis et religionis, spiritus eum replebit timoris dei. Christum enim in floris figura ostendit, oriturum ei uirga profecta de radice Iesse, id est uirgine generis Dauid, filii Iesse, in quo Christo consistere haberet tota substantia spiritus, non quasi postea obueutura illi, qui semper spiritus dei fuerit, ante carnem quoque, - ne ex hoc argumenteris prophetiam ad eum Christum pertinere, qui ut homo tantum ex solo censu Dauid postea consecuturus sit dei sui spiritum, — sed quoniam exinde, quo floruisset in carne sumpta ex stirpe Dauid, requiescere in illo haberet omnis operatio gratiae spiritalis et concessare et finem facere, quantum ad Iudaeos; sicut et res ipsa testatur, nihil exinde spirante penes illos spiritu creatoris, ablato a Iudaea sapiente et prudente architecto et consiliario et propheta, ut hoc sit: lex et prophetae usque ad Iohannem. accipe nunc, quomodo et a Christo in caelum recepto charismata obuentura pronuntiarit: ascendit in sublimitatem, id est in caelum; captiuam duxit captiuitatem, id est mortem uel humanam seruitutem; data dedit filiis hominum, id est donatiua, quae charismata dicimus. eleganter \'filiis hominum\' ait, non passim (hominibus\\ nos ostendens filios hominum, id est uere hominum, apostolorum. in euangelio enim, inquit, ego uos generaui, et: filii mei, quos parturio rursus, iam nunc et illa promissio spiritus absoluta, facta per Iohelem: in nouissimis temporibus effundam de meo spiritu in omnem carnem, et prophetabunt filii filiaeque eorum, et super seruos et ancillas meas de meo spiritu -effundam. et utique si in nouissimos dies gratiam spiritus creator repromisit, Christus autem spiritalium dispensator in nouissimis diebus apparuit dicente apostolo: at ubi tempus expletum est, misit deus filium suum, et rursus: quia tempus iam in collecto est, apparet et de temporum ultimorum praedicatione hanc gratiam spiritus ad Christum praedicatoris pertinere. compara denique species apostoli et Esaiae. alii, inquit, datur per spiritum sermo sapientiae: statim et Esaias sapientiae spiritum posuit; alii sermo scientiae: hic erit sermo intellegentiae et consilii; alii fides in eodem spiritu: hic erit spiritus religionis et timoris dei; alii donum curationum, alii uirtutum: hic erit ualentiae spiritus; alii prophetia, alii distinctio spirituum, alii genera linguarum, alii interpretatio linguarum: hic erit agnitionis spiritus. uide apostolum et in distributione facienda unius spiritus et in specialitate interpretanda prophetae conspirantem. possum dicere: ipsum quod corporis nostri per multa et diuersa membra unitatem charismatum uariorum compagini adaequauit, eundem et corporis humani et spiritus sancti dominum ostendit, qui merita charismatum noluerit esse in corpore spiritus, quae nec (membrorum) in corpore humano collocauit, qui de dilectione quoque omnibus charismatibus praeponenda apostolum instruxerit principali praecepto quod probauit et Christus: diliges dominum de totis praecordiis et totis uiribus et tota anima et proximum tibi tamquam te. et si quod in lege scriptum esset commemorat in aliis linguis et in aliis labiis locuturum creatorem, cum hac commemoratione charisma linguarum confirmat, nec hic potest uideri alienum charisma creatoris praedicatione confirmasse. aeque praescribens silentium mulieribus in ecclesia, ne quid discendi dumtaxat gratia loquantur, — ceterum prophetandi ius et illas habere iam ostendit, cum mulieri etiam prophetanti uelamen imponit — ex lege accipit subiciendae feminae auctoritatem, quam, ut semel dixerim, nosse non debuit nisi in destructionem. Sed ut iam a spiritalibus recedamus, res ipsae probare debebunt, quis nostrum temere deo suo uindicet et an nostrae parti possit opponi haec, et si creator repromisit in suum Christum nondum reuelatum, ut Iudaeis tantum destinatum, suas habitura in suo tempore in suo Christo et in suo populo operationes. exhibeat itaque Marcion dei sui dona, aliquos prophetas, qui tamen non de humano sensu, sed de dei spiritu sint locuti, qui et futura praenuntiarint et cordis occulta traduxerint; edat aliquem psalmum, aliquam uisionem, aliquam orationem, dumtaxat spiritalem, in ecstasi, id est in amentia, si qua linguae interpretatio accessit; probet mihi etiam mulierem apud se prophetasse ex illis suis sanctioribus feminis magnis, dicam: si haec omnia facilius a me proferuntur et utique conspirantia regulis et dispositionibus et disciplinis creatoris, sine dubio dei mei erit et Christus et spiritus et apostolus. habet professionem meam qui uoluerit eam exigere.
pass_a_gloss: The head of the man is Christ. Who is Christ? He who is not the author of the man? For 'head' is applied to authority, and authority will not be of another than the author. Of which man, then, is He the head? Certainly of Him about whom He subjoins: for the man ought not to be veiled, since he is the image of God. Therefore, if he is the image of the Creator — for He, looking at His own Word, was going to make man: 'Let us make,' He says, 'man in our image and likeness' — how can I have another head, not Him whose image I am? For when I am the image of the Creator, there is no place in me for another head. But also, why ought the woman to have power over her head? If it is because she was made from the man and for the man according to the institution of the Creator, so also the Apostle took care of His discipline, interpreting the causes of discipline from His institution. He also adds: 'because of the angels.' Which ones? That is, of which one? If the apostate angels of the Creator, rightly, so that the face which scandalized them might refer to a certain mark of humility and obscuration of beauty; if, however, because of the angels of another God, why does he fear, if not even the Marcionites themselves desire women? We have often shown that heresies are placed among evils as an evil by the Apostle and that those who flee heresies as an evil are to be approved. Accordingly, we have already proven in the Gospel the truth of the body and blood of the Lord concerning the sacrament of bread and cup against the phantom of Marcion, but also that every mention of judgment belongs to the Creator, as to the judging God, has been treated almost throughout the whole work. Now concerning spiritual things. I say these things, too, which were promised by the Creator in Christ, under that prescription, most just, I think, by which the exhibition of another is not to be believed except of Him whose promise has been proven. Isaiah pronounced: 'A rod will come forth from the root of Jesse, and a flower will ascend from the rod, and the Spirit of God will rest upon Him.' Then he enumerates the species: the Spirit of wisdom and intelligence, the Spirit of counsel and strength, the Spirit of knowledge and piety, the Spirit of fear of God will fill Him. For He shows Christ in the figure of a flower, to arise from the rod which has come forth from the root of Jesse, that is, from the virgin of the race of David, the son of Jesse, in whom Christ was to have the whole substance of the Spirit, not as if it were to be given to Him afterwards, who always was the Spirit of God, even before the flesh, — lest you argue from this that the prophecy pertains to that Christ who, as a man only, was to receive the Spirit of his God afterwards, from the sole stock of David, — but since from that time on, when He had flourished in the flesh taken from the stock of David, every operation of spiritual grace was to rest in Him and to be given and to be finished, as far as the Jews are concerned; just as the fact itself testifies, nothing from that time on breathing the Spirit of the Creator among them, with the wise and prudent architect and counselor and prophet taken away from Judea, so that this is: 'the law and the prophets until John.' Receive now how He also pronounced, when Christ was received into heaven, the charisms which were to come: 'He ascended into the height,' that is, into heaven; 'He led captivity captive,' that is, death or human servitude; 'He gave gifts to the sons of men,' that is, the gifts which we call charisms. He elegantly says 'to the sons of men,' not to men in general, showing us the sons of men, that is, the true men, the Apostles. For in the Gospel, He says: 'I have begotten you,' and: 'My sons, whom I beget again,' and already now that promise of the Spirit is fulfilled, which was made through Joel: 'In the last days I will pour out my Spirit upon all flesh, and your sons and your daughters will prophesy, and upon my servants and my handmaids I will pour out my Spirit.' And certainly, if in the last days the Creator promised the grace of His Spirit, but Christ, the dispenser of spiritual things, appeared in the last days, as the Apostle says: 'But when the time was fulfilled, God sent His Son,' and again: 'Because the time is already gathered,' it appears that this grace of the Spirit pertains to Christ, the preacher, concerning the preaching of the last times. Compare, finally, the species of the Apostle and Isaiah. 'To others,' he says, 'is given the word of wisdom through the Spirit;' immediately Isaiah also placed the Spirit of wisdom; 'to others the word of knowledge;' this will be the word of intelligence and counsel; 'to others faith in the same Spirit;' this will be the Spirit of piety and fear of God; 'to others the gift of healings, to others of virtues;' this will be the Spirit of strength; 'to others prophecy, to others the distinction of spirits, to others kinds of tongues, to others the interpretation of tongues;' this will be the Spirit of knowledge. See the Apostle conspiring with the prophet both in making the distribution of one Spirit and in interpreting the specialty. I can say: the same One who has adapted the unity of the various charisms to the diversity of the many members of our body shows Himself to be the Lord both of the human body and of the Holy Spirit, who did not want the merits of the charisms to be in the Spirit, which He did not even place in the human body, who also instructed the Apostle to prefer love to all charisms with a principal precept which Christ also approved: 'You will love the Lord with all your heart and with all your strength and with all your soul and your neighbor as yourself.' And if He recalls something written in the law, that the Creator will speak in other languages and in other lips, with this recollection He confirms the charism of languages, nor can it be seen here that the charism of the Creator is alien, having confirmed the preaching. Equally, prescribing silence to women in the church, lest they speak for the sake of learning only, — nevertheless, He has already shown that they also have the right of prophesying, when He puts a veil on a prophesying woman — He takes the authority of subjecting the woman from the law, which, as I have said once, he ought not to have known except for destruction. But so that we may now recede from spiritual things, the facts themselves ought to prove who of us rashly vindicates his God and whether this can be opposed to our side, and if the Creator promised in His Christ, not yet revealed, as destined only for the Jews, that He would have His operations in His Christ and in His people in His time. Therefore, let Marcion exhibit the gifts of his God, some prophets who have spoken not from human sense but from the Spirit of God, who have also foretold the future and revealed the hidden things of the heart; let him produce some psalm, some vision, some spiritual prayer, at least in ecstasy, that is, in madness, if some interpretation of language has been added; let him also prove to me that a woman has prophesied among his people, from those more holy women of his, I will say: if all these things are more easily produced by me and certainly conspiring with the rules and dispositions and disciplines of the Creator, without doubt, the Christ and the Spirit and the Apostle will be of my God. He who wishes can exact my profession.

pass_b_english: Christ is the head of the man. But who is Christ? Is He not the author of the man? 'Head' implies authority, and authority belongs to no one but the author. So of which man is He the head? Certainly the one Paul goes on to discuss: the man ought not to be veiled, because he is the image of God. If he is the image of the Creator — who, looking at His own Word about to make man, said, 'Let us make man in our image and likeness' (Gen 1:26) — how can I have any other head than the One whose image I am? When I am the Creator's image, there is no room in me for another head. But then why must the woman have a symbol of authority on her head? If it is because she was made from the man and for the man according to the Creator's institution, then the Apostle also enforced His discipline, deriving the reasons for that discipline from His institution. Paul adds: 'because of the angels.' Which angels? That is, whose angels? If they are the apostate angels of the Creator, then rightly so, so that the face which scandalized them might bear a mark of humility and the veiling of beauty. But if they belong to another God, what is there to fear, when not even the Marcionites themselves desire women? We have often shown that the Apostle ranks heresies among evils as an evil, and that those who flee heresies as an evil are to be approved. Accordingly, we have already proven in the Gospel the truth of the Lord's body and blood in the sacrament of bread and cup against Marcion's phantom, and also that every mention of judgment belongs to the Creator as the judging God — a point treated almost throughout the whole work. Now concerning spiritual gifts. I say these things, too, which were promised in Christ by the Creator, under that rule — most just, I think — that no one's manifestation is to be believed except His whose promise has been proven. Isaiah declared: 'A shoot will spring from the stump of Jesse, a branch from his roots will bear fruit, and the Spirit of the Lord will rest on Him — the Spirit of wisdom and understanding, the Spirit of counsel and might, the Spirit of knowledge and the fear of the Lord' (Isa 11:1-2). He then lists the Spirit's species: wisdom, intelligence, counsel, strength, knowledge, piety, and the Spirit of the fear of God filling Him. Isaiah portrays Christ as the flower rising from the shoot that comes from the root of Jesse — that is, from the virgin of David's line, Jesse's son — in whom Christ was to possess the whole substance of the Spirit, not as something added later to One who was always the Spirit of God even before the flesh. Otherwise you might argue the prophecy refers to a Christ who, as mere man from David's stock, would only later receive the Spirit of His God. Rather, from the moment He blossomed in the flesh taken from David's line, every operation of spiritual grace was to rest in Him, be dispensed, and reach its completion as far as the Jews were concerned — just as the facts prove: from that time on, nothing breathed the Creator's Spirit among them, once the wise architect, prudent counselor, and prophet had been taken from Judea, so that 'the Law and the Prophets were until John.' Now see how He also foretold the charisms that would come after Christ was received into heaven: 'He ascended on high,' that is, into heaven; 'He led captivity captive,' that is, death or human bondage; 'He gave gifts to the sons of men' — the gifts we call charisms. He says 'sons of men' elegantly, not 'men' indiscriminately, pointing us to the true sons of men, the Apostles. For in the Gospel He says: 'I have begotten you,' and 'My sons, whom I am begetting again.' And already now that promise of the Spirit is fulfilled, spoken through Joel: 'In the last days I will pour out My Spirit on all flesh; your sons and daughters will prophesy, and on My servants and handmaids I will pour out My Spirit' (Joel 2:28-29). And certainly, if the Creator promised the grace of His Spirit for the last days, but Christ, the dispenser of spiritual things, appeared in the last days — as the Apostle says: 'When the time had fully come, God sent His Son,' and again: 'The time is already gathered up' — it follows that this grace of the Spirit belongs to Christ the Preacher, in the preaching of the last times. Finally, compare the Apostle's list with Isaiah's. Paul says: 'To one is given through the Spirit a word of wisdom' — and immediately Isaiah sets the Spirit of wisdom; 'to another a word of knowledge' — here is the Spirit of intelligence and counsel; 'to another faith by the same Spirit' — here is the Spirit of piety and fear of God; 'to another gifts of healing, to another workings of miracles' — here is the Spirit of strength; 'to another prophecy, to another distinguishing of spirits, to another kinds of tongues, to another interpretation of tongues' — here is the Spirit of knowledge. See the Apostle conspiring with the prophet both in distributing the one Spirit and in specifying the gifts. I can say: the same One who adapted the unity of diverse charisms to the many members of our body shows Himself Lord of both the human body and the Holy Spirit — who did not want the merits of charisms to reside in the Spirit, any more than He placed them in the human body, and who also taught the Apostle to prefer love above all charisms by the principal commandment that Christ Himself endorsed: 'You shall love the Lord with all your heart, with all your strength, and with all your soul, and your neighbor as yourself.' And when Paul recalls something written in the Law — that the Creator would speak in other tongues and through other lips — he confirms the charism of tongues by that very recollection; nor can the Creator's charism appear alien here, confirmed as it is by the preaching. Likewise, prescribing silence for women in the church, lest they speak merely for the sake of learning — though He has already shown they also have the right to prophesy, when He requires a veil on a prophesying woman — He takes the authority for the woman's subjection from the Law, which, as I have said once, he ought not to have known except to destroy it. But now that we turn from spiritual things, the facts themselves must prove which of us rashly claims his God, and whether this can be opposed to our side. If the Creator promised in His Christ, not yet revealed, destined only for the Jews, that He would have His operations in His Christ and His people in His time, then let Marcion produce the gifts of his god: some prophets who spoke not from human sense but from God's Spirit, who foretold the future and exposed the heart's secrets; let him produce a psalm, a vision, a spiritual prayer — at least in ecstasy, that is, madness — if any interpretation of tongues has been added; let him also prove that a woman has prophesied among his people, from those holier women of his. I say: if all these things are more easily produced by me and certainly align with the Creator's rules, dispositions, and disciplines, then without doubt the Christ, the Spirit, and the Apostle belong to my God. Anyone who wishes may demand my profession.

review.notes: All clauses in the Latin source were checked against Pass A and Pass B. Scripture citations (Genesis 1:26, Isaiah 11:1-2, Joel 2:28-29) were correctly identified and added to the English text. The translation preserves the nuances of agency and theological distinctions (e.g., the distinction between the Creator and the 'other' God).
